theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (+1.13%) and Health Care (+0.49%) led the market today, while Technology (-6.27%) and Industrials (-2.88%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -3.37% versus +0.57% for defensives and -1.20% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -1.50% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -4.66%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up -1.94%, outperforming large caps. The VIX rose 16.33% to 33.12, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.47% to $3,516.50, crude oil was little changed at $83.17, and bitcoin slipped 6.44% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
